analysis:
Examined all supplied source, patches and metadata against the indexed model and selected T-041 detail. StartupPreload.swift:299-305 now queues memory/slot-deferred candidates for selected-model recovery, guarded against cancellation, shutdown and an explicitly stopped preload. It does not directly change weight binding, cache crypto, routing authorization or self-test retirement. Integration must examine ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery: selection filtering, bounded retry/backoff, authoritative memory/no-eviction admission, failed-self-test exclusion and shutdown cancellation remain outside this evidence (TB-007, T-012/T-027, T-029, T-041).
StartupShutdown.swift:60,68-95 replaces exhaustive unload completion with a 15-second per-slot wait and permits retained slots and ongoing unload tasks when cleanup returns true. Existing serving drain, local endpoint stop, App Attest worker stop, coordinator shutdown and native MiMo owner drain remain before teardown (lines 24-59). This improves termination availability, but integration must verify that callers treat success as terminal shutdown rather than permission to restart serving in the same process, and that MLX cache clearing at line 62 is safe while an unload/native retirement remains outstanding. Actual process exit and unloadModel/native reclamation contracts are not supplied; retained memory alone does not establish a new disclosure or unsafe reclamation (T-028, T-010, T-043, TB-007).
Testing.swift adds internal recovery override/wait seams at head patch lines 514-525, consistent with existing internal test access; no new remote or public entry point is shown. No independently supported security regression qualifies in this scope. Remaining recovery and terminal-shutdown contracts materially affect the conclusion and require cross-file integration review.
